english.title: Aid / abet a person to threaten another with an offensive weapon in a public place
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) **(..SPECIFY PERSON..) had with

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_

an offensive weapon, namely **(..SPECIFY WEAPON..), in a public place, namely **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..), and you aided, abetted, counselled or procured,

(C)_[him]_
(D)_[her]_

to unlawfully and intentionally threaten another person, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON THREATENED..), with that weapon in such a way that a reasonable person who was exposed to the same threat would think that there was an immediate risk of physical harm to that reasonable person
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1A(1) and (4) of the Prevention of Crime Act 1953 and section 8 of the Accessories and Abettors Act 1861.

english.notes:
(i) Section 1A(3) defines 'public place' and 'offensive weapon' to have the same meaning as in section 1. Section 1(4) defines 'public place' as any highway and any other premises or place to which at the material time the public have or are permitted to have access, whether on payment or otherwise. 'offensive weapon' means any article made or adapted for use for causing injury to the person, or intended by the person having it with him for such use by him, or by some other person.
(ii) The court may find the defendant not guilty of this offence but guilty of an offence under section 1 of the Act, see offence wording H7979.
(iii) The Offensive Weapons Act 2019 amended the offence to include an objective element - whether a reasonable person exposed to the threat would think there was an immediate risk of physical harm. For offences committed before 6th April 2022 see H10671.

other.penalty:
Either waySummary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 1A4(a) and (8) of the Prevention of Crime Act 1953 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.

For minimum sentence for this offence see section 312 of the Sentencing Act 2020.
